title: Introduce lightweight pulse smoke runner, trim harness deps, and publish stability playbook
creator: Sanjay Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our full regression harness takes too long to iterate on for day-to-day stability checks, and the dependency graph for several adapters (legacy Kafka proxy, monorepo shim layers) increases CI flakiness and security upgrade surface. This ticket creates a small, well-documented 'pulse' smoke runner for quick end-to-end validation, prunes and pins transitive dependencies in the perf harness, and publishes a stability playbook for on-call and QA to follow when regressions surface.

Scope:
- Implement a lightweight runner (pulse-smoke) that runs a representative 30s workload across core adapters (http/gRPC/streaming) with deterministic seeding and metrics export.
- Remove or replace two fragile adapter shims (legacy-kafka-proxy, node-load-adapter) in CI smoke paths; keep for full regression but not for pulse runs.
- Upgrade critical dependencies (protobuf, grpc libs, test-framework) to latest patched versions and pin transitive versions in a lockfile.
- Add a stability playbook (short-form runbook) describing investigative steps, dashboards to check, and rollback guidance for model-serving perf regressions.

Why this matters: Faster feedback loops reduce classifier drift cascades and shorten mean-time-to-detection for perf regressions. Reducing dependency churn and CI surface area reduces flakes and security exposure.
acceptance_criteria: pulse-smoke runner is runnable locally and in CI via ./tools/pulse-smoke with a <60s wall time by default
pulse run produces a stable metrics artifact (Prometheus pushgateway + JSON summary) and exits non-zero on latency or error thresholds
legacy-kafka-proxy and node-load-adapter are removed from the CI smoke matrix and documented as remaining in full-regression only
dependency lockfile added to repo and CI enforces lockfile parity; protobuf and grpc major versions bumped and release notes recorded
stability playbook checked into docs/ and linked from Console incident templates
implementation_steps: Design pulse-smoke runner API and seed strategy (deterministic corpus, short sequences)
Implement runner harness in Rust shim (reusing existing micro-runner libs) and expose a small CLI wrapper
Add CI job 'smoke:pulse' and remove fragile adapters from smoke matrix; leave full-regression job unchanged
Audit deps via cargo/poetry/npm-tooling, update protobuf/grpc/test-framework to patched releases, and commit lockfile
Author stability playbook and example incident walkthrough; circulate to on-call and QA for review
Ship change behind a feature flag and enable for non-prod CI for one cycle, gather flakiness metrics, then flip in main branch
